items.en: to come to know / find out
items.ex: 친구 덕분에 한국 문화를 알게 되었어요.
다음 달부터 한국 회사에서 일하게 됐어요.

bg-26-01.hint: I ended up working at a Korean company.
bg-26-01.why: -게 되다 expresses a change in situation due to external factors: 일하- + -게 됐어요.

bg-26-01.q: Express that you have come to like Korean food. Use 한국 음식 + object particle -을/를 and 좋아하다 + -게 되다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-26-01.why: -게 되다 indicates a change in state or habit over time: 좋아하- + -게 됐어요.

steps.en: I ended up working at a company.
I ended up working at a Korean company.

ko: 하지만 한국 친구들을 사귀면서 한국 문화를 자연스럽게 알게 됐어요.
다음 달부터는 서울에 있는 회사에서 일하게 됐어요.
en: At first, I didn't know Korean well.
However, as I made Korean friends, I naturally came to know Korean culture.
Starting next month, I ended up working at a company in Seoul.

bg-26-01.q: How did the speaker come to know Korean culture?
bg-26-01.why: The text says '한국 친구들을 사귀면서 한국 문화를 자연스럽게 알게 됐어요'.

bg-26-01.q: What will the speaker do starting next month?
options: Work at a company in Seoul
bg-26-01.why: The text states '다음 달부터는 서울에 있는 회사에서 일하게 됐어요'.

items: Describe changes in personal situation using -게 되다
Explain how new circumstances or habits developed naturally over time

bg-26-02.why: The adjective 따뜻하다 takes -게 to become the adverb 따뜻하게 (warmly), modifying 입으세요.

bg-26-02.q: Wish someone an enjoyable meal for lunch. Use 점심, adverbial form 맛있다 + -게, and honorific 드시다 + -(으)세요.
bg-26-02.why: 맛있다 combines with -게 to form the polite adverbial wish 맛있게 드세요.

steps.en: Because the weather is cold, please dress warmly.

ko: 그래서 외출할 때 옷을 따뜻하게 입었어요.
친구들과 식당에서 만나서 점심도 맛있게 먹었어요.
en: So when going out, I dressed warmly.
I met my friends at a restaurant and ate lunch deliciously too.

bg-26-02.q: Why did the writer dress warmly when going out?
options: Because they were at home all day
bg-26-02.why: The text explains '오늘 날씨가 아주 쌀쌀해요. 그래서 외출할 때 옷을 따뜻하게 입었어요'.

bg-26-02.q: What did the writer do with friends?
options: Ate lunch deliciously at a restaurant
bg-26-02.why: The text states '친구들과 식당에서 만나서 점심도 맛있게 먹었어요'.

items: Convert adjectives into descriptive adverbs by attaching -게
Use common friendly expressions like 맛있게 드세요 and 따뜻하게 입으세요

bg-26-03.why: 크다 becomes the adverb 크게 when modifying 말씀해 주세요.

bg-26-03.q: Politely ask someone to explain the grammar easily. Use 문법 + -을/를, adverbial form 쉽다 (ㅂ irregular) + -게, and 설명하다 + -아/어 주세요.
bg-26-03.why: The adverb 쉽게 modifies the request verb 설명해 주세요.

bg-26-03.wrong: 잘 안 들리니까 조금 더 큰 말씀해 주세요.
answers: 잘 안 들리니까 조금 더 크게 말씀해 주세요.
잘 안 들리니까 조금 더 크게 말씀해 주세요
bg-26-03.hint: Modify the verb 말씀하다 with an adverb form: 크다 → 크게, not the adjective modifier 큰.
bg-26-03.why: To modify a verb (말씀하다), use the adverb ending -게: 크게 말씀해 주세요.

steps.en: Since I can't hear well, please speak a little louder.

ko: 한국어 수업 시간에 선생님께서 문법을 쉽게 설명해 주셨어요.
뒤에 앉은 친구가 잘 안 들려서 조금 더 크게 말해 달라고 부탁했어요.
선생님은 웃으면서 더 크고 또렷하게 말씀하셨어요.
en: In Korean class, the teacher explained the grammar easily.
A friend sitting in the back couldn't hear well and asked them to speak a little louder.
The teacher smiled and spoke louder and more clearly.

bg-26-03.q: How did the teacher explain the grammar in class?
bg-26-03.why: The text says '선생님께서 문법을 쉽게 설명해 주셨어요'.

bg-26-03.q: Why did the friend in the back ask the teacher to speak louder?
bg-26-03.why: The text says '뒤에 앉은 친구가 잘 안 들려서 조금 더 크게 말해 달라고 부탁했어요'.

items: Form adverbs from descriptive adjectives like 크다, 쉽다, and 짧다
Make polite requests asking others to speak louder or explain easily

bg-26-04.hint: I ended up going on a business trip.
bg-26-04.why: -게 되다 emphasizes that the business trip came about due to company circumstances rather than personal choice.

bg-26-04.q: Express a personal resolution to exercise every day for your health. Use 매일 운동 and 하다 + -기로 했어요.
bg-26-04.why: -기로 하다 indicates an active personal decision or resolution: 운동하- + -기로 했어요.

bg-26-04.wrong: 회사 일 때문에 다음 달에 서울로 이사하기로 되었어요.
answers: 회사 일 때문에 다음 달에 서울로 이사하게 되었어요.
회사 일 때문에 다음 달에 서울로 이사하게 됐어요.
회사 일 때문에 다음 달에 서울로 이사하게 되었어요
bg-26-04.hint: For changes resulting from external circumstances (회사 일 때문에), use -게 되다, not -기로 되다.
bg-26-04.why: The pattern for situational outcome is -게 되다: 이사하게 되었어요.

bg-26-04.h: External Circumstance -게 되다 vs Personal Decision -기로 하다

a.d: Expresses that a situation changed or happened due to outside circumstances, organizational decisions, or natural flow (*“ended up doing...”*).
ex: 회사 일로 외국에 **가게 되었어요**. / I ended up going abroad for company business.
친구 소개로 그분을 **알게 되었어요**. / I came to know that person through a friend.

b.d: Expresses an active personal choice, resolution, or mutual appointment (*“decided to do...”*).
ex: 건강을 위해 매일 운동을 **하기로 했어요**. / I decided to exercise every day for my health.
주말에 친구와 영화를 **보기로 했어요**. / I agreed to watch a movie with a friend this weekend.

bg-26-04.tip: Ask yourself 'Who decided this?' If it's a personal resolve or agreed plan, use -기로 하다; if circumstances led to the result, use -게 되다.

base.en: I ended up going on a business trip.

steps.en: I ended up going on a business trip to Korea.
Because of company business, I ended up going on a business trip to Korea.

ko: 회사 사정으로 갑자기 해외 지사로 출장을 가게 되었어요.
그래서 이번 주말에 친구를 만나려던 약속은 다음으로 미루기로 했어요.
친구에게 사정을 설명하고 다음에 꼭 맛있는 밥을 사기로 했어요.
en: Due to company circumstances, I suddenly ended up going on a business trip to an overseas branch.
So I decided to postpone my plans to meet my friend this weekend until next time.
I explained the situation to my friend and agreed to buy them a delicious meal next time.

bg-26-04.q: Why is the speaker going on a business trip?
options: Because they wanted a long vacation
To visit family for a wedding
bg-26-04.why: The passage begins '회사 사정으로 갑자기 해외 지사로 출장을 가게 되었어요'.

bg-26-04.q: What did the speaker decide to do regarding the weekend plan with their friend?
options: Invite the friend to the business trip
bg-26-04.why: The text says '친구를 만나려던 약속은 다음으로 미루기로 했어요'.

items: Distinguish situational results (-게 되다) from personal resolutions (-기로 하다)
Explain business appointments and scheduled commitments appropriately
